title: Nvidia's Kumo Relational predicts from a database without a training run
friendlyTitle: Nvidia's Kumo Relational predicts from a database without a training run
summary: Nvidia has introduced Kumo Relational, a pre-trained model that answers predictive questions directly on a relational database. You describe the question in its Predictive Query Language. The model gathers up to 10,000 historical examples as context and returns a prediction in one forward pass, without task-specific training or flattening the tables into one feature row. Nvidia says that across 41 tasks on 15 databases it beat supervised relational deep-learning models and expert-engineered gradient-boosted trees, and that on the SAP SALT benchmark it beat AutoGluon ensembles by 8 percent in mean reciprocal rank. It is available through Nvidia's open-source structured-data library or as an Nvidia NIM. The paper is on arXiv.
friendlySummary: Nvidia has introduced Kumo Relational, a pre-trained model that answers prediction questions directly on a relational database. You describe the question in its Predictive Query Language. The model gathers up to 10,000 past examples as context and returns a prediction in one pass. It does not need a separate training run for that task, and it does not need you to flatten the tables into one row of features. Nvidia says that across 41 tasks on 15 databases it beat supervised relational deep-learning models and expert-built gradient-boosted trees. On the SAP SALT benchmark, it beat AutoGluon ensembles by 8 percent in mean reciprocal rank. It is available through Nvidia's open-source structured-data library, or as an Nvidia NIM. The paper is on arXiv.
whyItMatters: Churn, demand, and fraud models often wait on weeks of feature engineering before anyone can ask a new question. A query against the database you already have is a faster first pass, if the tables are clean and you treat Nvidia's benchmarks as Nvidia's. It does not replace a check against your own held-out outcomes. An agent can call the same query, which means the prediction can land in a workflow before a person has looked at it.
